page_title: SQL style guide by Simon Holywell

summary.title: SQL style guide by Simon Holywell
summary.one_liner: A set of opinionated SQL formatting and naming conventions covering identifiers, keyword casing, whitespace "river" alignment, joins, subqueries, data types, and constraints.
keywords: sql table naming plural or collective
takeaways: Pick one SQL style and apply it consistently; use descriptive snake_case names without prefixes like tbl_ or sp_, and prefer singular column names and collective table names.
Write reserved keywords in uppercase, align root keywords on a shared 'river' so implementation details are left-aligned, and put newlines before AND/OR.
Use ANSI standard functions and keywords, SQL-92 double quotes for any quoted identifiers, and ISO 8601 for date/time values to aid portability.
Use NUMERIC or DECIMAL rather than REAL or FLOAT unless floating point is strictly needed; define keys and named constraints with CHECK ranges and clear layout.
Avoid designs such as EAV tables, splitting one logical table across many, and storing values and units in separate columns.
summary.summary: This is a community style guide for writing SQL, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and designed to be compatible with Joe Celko's SQL Programming Style book while being more opinionated and succinct. It is organised as rules with short Do/Avoid lists and concrete code examples covering general practice, naming conventions and uniform suffixes, query layout (keyword casing, whitespace, joins, subqueries, CASE/BETWEEN/IN preferences), CREATE TABLE layout, data type choice, keys and constraints, and designs to avoid. The appendix lists reserved keywords across ANSI SQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and Oracle, plus a set of suggested portable column data types.
